description: User-supplied Python+Rust design-experiment prototypes (kovan_semantics_prototype.py, lib.rs, test_prototype.py, then a richer 'populated' set: README.md, kovan_semantics_populated.rs, kovan_semantics_populated.py, test_populated.py) sketch a typed graph of scientific/engineering concepts (reactor types, neutronics approximations, TH conservation laws, ...) and relationships (SpecializationOf, ApproximationOf, DerivedFrom, ...) with alias-based resolution, intended eventually for the KOVAN mindmap/knowledge-graph views. User's detailed follow-up instruction (not the raw prototypes) is the actual spec: preserve existing kovan-semantics public API; domain-specific compiled enums (CoreConcept trait) for curated/foundational concepts only, with explicit stable string IDs independent of Rust variant names and static alias slices; everything else (facility models, software, benchmark models, literature/document nodes) as runtime-extensible User/Literature-origin concepts that never mutate the compiled core; treat aliases as concept metadata, never edges; typed Relation enum (21 variants, the ScaledFrom variant from the earliest prototype deliberately dropped per the user's precise dictated list) with precise per-variant Rustdoc + a separate GUI-facing label(); an Origin tag (Core/User/Literature) distinguishing provenance; a RelationStatus (Established/Provisional) so unvetted relationships stay visibly provisional; richer EdgeDetail payloads (Applicability: assumptions+validity ranges; VerificationRecord: benchmark+result+acceptance criterion) for the relation families that need them (Approximation/Simplifies/ReducedFrom/SurrogateOf family; Benchmark/Verified/Validated/Compared family) rather than flattening into generic strings. No coupling to the kovan crate/GUI/mindmap in this pass -- deterministic, AI-independent, usable by autocomplete/literature/codegen/future graph-viz. Populated example corpus (Ong dissertation / IAEA TECDOC-1694 / TUAS-paper-flavoured, illustrative only, no fabricated numeric results) as a test fixture, not shipped as an authoritative ontology.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented crates/kovan-semantics/src/ontology.rs (new module, ~750 lines incl. tests+docs): Relation (21 variants exactly matching the user's precise dictated list -- the ScaledFrom variant from the earliest raw prototype deliberately dropped, per-variant Rustdoc + a separate label() GUI string), RelationStatus (Established/Provisional), Origin (Core/User/Literature), Applicability + VerificationRecord (richer EdgeDetail payloads for the approximation and verification/validation relation families instead of flattening into Vec<String>), CoreConcept trait (explicit per-variant stable id(), independent of Rust variant names) implemented by three curated domain enums (Reactor, Neutronics, ThermalHydraulics), Concept/ConceptEdge (owned runtime records), ConceptGraph (BTreeMap-backed for deterministic iteration; add_core/add_user_concept/add_literature_concept/relate/relate_with/resolve/outgoing/incoming), ResolveOutcome (Found/Ambiguous/NotFound, distinguishing no-match from multi-match for a future autocomplete UI). resolve() is plain deterministic string normalization (lowercase+alphanumeric-only), no AI/heuristics. add_user_concept/add_literature_concept reject a duplicate id (including a core one) rather than overwrite -- the compiled core is never mutated by a runtime insert. Zero dependency on the kovan crate/GUI/mindmap, zero new external crate deps (std only) -- self-contained per the user's explicit instruction. Re-exported from lib.rs alongside the existing public API, nothing renamed/removed (existing API fully preserved). Test fixture sample_ontology() (test-only, not shipped as pub API, per the user's own 'not an authoritative complete ontology' framing) spans all 3 core domains + 22 user concepts (facility models, software, numerical methods) + 3 literature-origin document concepts (Ong dissertation / IAEA TECDOC-1694 / TUAS paper flavoured, illustrative naming only -- no fabricated numeric benchmark results anywhere, consistent with this workspace's data-integrity rules), 34 edges covering 19 of 21 relation types (ParameterizedBy and Contradicts covered in a separate small synthetic-graph test instead, to avoid asserting a false 'these real benchmarks contradict' claim). 19 new tests covering exactly the required list: alias resolution (case/punctuation-insensitive, ambiguous vs not-found), canonical identity, graph directionality (outgoing vs incoming), cross-domain relationships, user extensions that never mutate the core, EdgeDetail richness, provisional-vs-established, GUI label round-trip. Verified: cargo check -p kovan-semantics --all-targets --all-features clean; cargo check -p kovan-semantics --lib --no-default-features clean; cargo test -p kovan-semantics --lib --release: 61 passed (19 new + 42 pre-existing), 0 failed; cargo check -p kovan (downstream consumer) still clean. Regenerated crates/kovan-semantics/docs/kovan-semantics-api.md via kovan-cli api-docs (rustdoc-md + nightly toolchain, both already installed) so the mirror doesn't go stale. Follow-up filed as op-2drr (TOML/Markdown ingestion into this API, deliberately deferred).

acceptance_criteria: Swapping pebble bed for prismatic requires no change outside the closure impl, verified by a compile-time test instantiating both. Dispatch is an enum match; grep confirms no Box<dyn>/&dyn/Arc<dyn> introduced in the closure or PowerConversion path. Adding a third variant produces compile errors at every match site.
description:
ARCHITECTURE REQUIREMENT: the core flow closure is the ONLY thing that differs between the two HTGR geometries. Everything else is shared - TRISO fuel model, graphite conduction, decay heat, PRKE, helium properties, RCCS radiation. What differs: pressure drop, wall heat transfer, effective conductivity.

DISPATCH IS SETTLED (maintainer, 2026-08-13): HARD ENUM. No dyn as far as possible.

  enum CoreFlowClosure { PebbleBed(PebbleBedClosure), Prismatic(PrismaticClosure) }

  - A trait MAY be used as a compiler-enforced CONTRACT on each concrete struct, so the compiler verifies every closure implements the required methods.
  - The trait is NOT used for runtime dispatch. Match on the enum.
  - No Box<dyn>, no &dyn, no Arc<dyn>.

This matches the workspace Rust design rules (enums give exhaustiveness - adding a geometry becomes a compile error at every match site, not a runtime surprise - plus zero heap allocation and working go-to-definition, which dyn breaks).

Same applies to PowerConversion (steam Rankine vs direct Brayton), which is the BOP-side analogue and will gain a Brayton variant under op-id3l.12.

Gated on the TAMPINES transonic HEM critical-flow V&V (op-id3l.15).
title: HTGR Phase 2.1: CoreFlowClosure and PowerConversion — HARD ENUM dispatch, no dyn

description: New workspace crate: Rust-first port of LIGGGHTS granular DEM. Reference: LIGGGHTS-PUBLIC and LAMMPS GRANULAR. Owns DEM, contact mechanics, granular/particle heat transfer, pebble-bed and packed-bed physics; future CFD-DEM coupling to OUTRAM-FOAM (op-2kk). One of the three Phase-II architectural pillars kept separate: (1) thermophysical properties [tampines], (2) CFD/multiphase [outram-foam], (3) DEM/granular [this]. Roadmap Phases 1-5 are child beads. Workspace hard rules apply: enum dispatch (no Box/dyn), no lifetime params (Arc/index ids), Arc<RwLock> for shared state, non-GUI lib must compile/run on Android/Termux, GPLv3-compatible with upstream provenance headers on any ported file. Definition of done per physics bead: theory docs + verification tests + reference-benchmark comparison + unit-safe uom; humans own physics/V&V/judgement. Trademark-compliant name follows the outram-park-fork-<project> convention (cf. op-ahi). Source: Theodore Ong, 'OUTRAM PARK Phase II Architecture', 2026-07-23 (rough; CLAUDE.md takes precedence).
